lines: Your heart is a muscle, about the size of your fist.
It beats around one hundred thousand times a day.
Inside, it is really two pumps, side by side.
The right side sends blood to your lungs, to pick up oxygen.
The left side sends that fresh blood to the rest of your body.
Between the rooms of the heart there are small doors, called valves.
They open one way only, so blood never flows back.
And the sound a doctor hears, lub dub, is those doors closing.
So every beat is the same short trip. Body, heart, lungs, heart, and body again.
And it never takes a break.
